payload.task: Self-diffusion coefficient of Cu in a perfect fcc Cu crystal at 300 K by molecular dynamics (property self_diffusion, cm2/s)
payload.reason: Premise check failed: the quantity cannot be measured with MD as posed. (1) In a perfect crystal (no vacancies, interstitials, or surfaces) there is no diffusion mechanism on any MD timescale. Atoms only vibrate about lattice sites, so the MSD levels off at a vibrational value of ~0.01-0.02 A^2 at 300 K. Fitting MSD/6t would give a number that falls toward zero as 1/t and depends only on run length. Concerted ring/exchange jumps cost even more energy than vacancy jumps and never occur at 300 K. (2) In real Cu, self-diffusion goes through thermal vacancies, with an activation energy of about 2 eV (formation + migration) and a prefactor of order 0.1-1 cm2/s. An Arrhenius estimate at 300 K gives D ~ 1e-36 to 1e-34 cm2/s. With a jump length of ~2.6 A, that means one jump per atom every ~1e18-1e20 s, far longer than the age of the universe. A ns-scale MD run, or any feasible run, would see zero jumps, so D = 0 within statistics and the run gives no information about the true value. (3) No measurement exists at 300 K either: tracer data are taken at roughly 700-1350 K and extrapolated. So there is also no independent reference at this temperature to validate against, and none in /data/calibration/tier1.json. Posting a number would mean reporting a run-length artifact as a material property. Well-posed alternatives I can run instead: (a) vacancy-mediated Cu self-diffusion at high temperature (e.g. 900-1300 K) from MD on a supercell with one explicit vacancy. Rescale by the equilibrium vacancy concentration exp(S_f/k)exp(-E_f/kT) from the same model, fit an Arrhenius law, and compare Q and D0 with tracer data in the measured range. If an extrapolated 300 K value is still wanted, report it as an extrapolation with orders-of-magnitude uncertainty, not as a direct MD result. (b) NEB vacancy migration barrier plus vacancy formation energy, giving D(T) through transition-state theory or kinetic Monte Carlo, again validated in the measured temperature range. (c) Self-diffusion of liquid Cu just above the melting point, where MD MSD is directly measurable in tens of ps. Validate the model first by recovering the Cu melting point of 1357.77 K (tier1.json, ITS-90) with coexistence MD.
